summary: Aggressive quantization profile applied -> elevated tail latency and decoding errors; request safe staged rollback and verification
description: Customer applied an experimental 'AggressiveQuant' profile to their Dedicated pool to reduce token cost. Within 30 minutes they reported a 2-3x increase in p95/p99 latency, sporadic 5xx decoder errors, and higher output divergence on a set of regression prompts. They want guidance for a safe, staged rollback that minimizes user-facing errors and avoids cache/kv corruption.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant applied quant_profile: AggressiveQuant via Console -> Model routing updated to use rw-infer-luminous-1.3-q4_0 (quantized) for route /v1/annotate
2) Autoscale and batching policies left at customer defaults (max_batch_size=64, concurrency=8), no manual worker restart
3) Within ~20-40 min traffic saw increased tail latency and occasional 5xx decoder exceptions in traces
4) Customer ran evaluation suite of 100 regression prompts and observed change-rate ~8% (higher than expected 0.5-1%)
logs: [2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] worker-7 WARN kernel-fallback: requested q4 kernel unsupported for seq_len=2048, falling back to slower kernel
[2026-03-12T14:18:02Z] routing: model variant change -> rw-infer-luminous-1.3-q4_0; batching metrics: p95 increased from 210ms to 520ms
investigation_notes: Support: initial triage indicates correlation between quant profile switch and p95 spike; logs show kernel fallback and sporadic decoder errors.
SRE: fallback to slower kernels for some sequence lengths when optimized quant kernels missing can explain tail latency increase but not decoder errors.
ML infra: quantization introduces subtle logits differences; combined with larger batch sizes and KV prefix caching can amplify decode divergence for some prompts.
Hypothesis: AggressiveQuant changed both kernel selection and runtime memory layout; combined with high max_batch_size and no staged rollout produced tail latency & rare decoding failures.
Risk: naive restart or cache flush could transiently increase 429s/throttling if capacity not warmed before traffic shift. Need rolling plan with warmup traffic and verification prompts.
requested_action: Provide a step-by-step, low-risk rollback plan to restore previous stable quantization profile and batching settings, including checks to validate output parity on the customer's regression prompt set. Advise any runtime flags or restart order to avoid KV-cache corruption.
proposed_rollback_plan: 1) Prepare: Collect exact prior model/version tag (rw-infer-luminous-1.3-release-202602) and current routing policy. Export customer's 50 regression prompts to a verification bundle.

2) Pin & route: Create a new routing policy that pins production traffic to the previous non-quantized variant (rw-infer-luminous-1.3-release-202602) but do NOT switch traffic immediately; set routing weight 0->10% staged.
3) Reduce batching: Temporarily lower max_batch_size to the previous baseline (32) and concurrency to 4 to avoid added tail latency during rollout.
4) Warmup: Send synthetic/warmup requests (small volume, controlled QPS) to newly pinned variant to populate kernels and JIT caches on workers.
5) Gradual traffic shift: Increase routed weight in steps (10 -> 30 -> 60 -> 100) over 5-10 minute windows while monitoring metrics and verification prompts after each step.

6) KV/prefix cache handling: Do NOT flush the customer prefix/kvcache globally; instead rely on worker warmup. If decoder errors persist, perform per-worker graceful restart in a rolling fashion (drain then restart) to avoid global cache wipe.
7) Autoscale adjustment: Disable aggressive scale-down during the rollback window to prevent capacity churn; allow scale-up if needed.

8) Post-rollback: Once 100% traffic routed to prior variant and verification prompts match thresholds, restore original batching/concurrency and re-enable autoscale. Record timestamps and create a short postmortem.

9) Follow-up: Recommend a staged canary procedure for future quant profile changes (0/1/10/30/100% with fixed verification triggers) and add the customer's regression set to Optimize's continuous evals.
verification_checks: Monitor p95 and p99 latency for /v1/annotate (baseline target: p95 < 300ms)
Run regression bundle after each traffic increment; target output-diff < 1% on exact-match metrics and human-checked quality on 10 hand-picked prompts
Observe kernel-fallback logs disappear for common seq_len buckets
Check worker restart logs for any kv-cache mismatch exceptions
resolution: Temporary staged rollback initiated by Support (routing pinned to rw-infer-luminous-1.3-release-202602 and batching reduced). Warmup completed; early verification bundle shows outputs within acceptable delta. Customer monitoring session scheduled for 2026-03-13 15:00 UTC to confirm final state. Pending full closure after 24h stability.
